recipes.name: Buttermilk Cinnamon Rolls
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Dissolve yeast in warm water in a large bowl. Let stand until creamy, about 10 minutes. Heat buttermilk in a small saucepan until warm to the touch.

Pour buttermilk and oil into the yeast mixture and mix well. Combine flour, salt, and baking soda. Stir the flour mixture into the liquid 1 cup at a time until a soft dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead 20 times. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes. Stir together butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl.

Roll dough out into a large rectangle on a lightly floured surface. Spread the brown sugar and butter mixture over the dough. Roll up into a log and pinch the seam to seal. Slice into 1-inch pieces and place cut-side up in a lightly greased 10x15-inch baking pan. Cover and let rise for 30 minutes, or refrigerate overnight. If baking immediately, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 to 25 minutes. Let stand for 2 to 3 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Buttermilk Cinnamon Rolls
raw_recipe.description: A light buttermilk yeast dough starts you off on the right foot for these gooey rolls filled with brown sugar, cinnamon and butter. Once assembled, they can be refrigerated overnight if need be, so you can wake up and pop them right in the oven.

video.description: What’s better than cinnamon rolls … buttermilk cinnamon rolls! These tasty treats are perfect for a weekend morning fresh out of the oven. They are soft, gooey, warm, and full of sweetness!

review.reviewBody: WONDERFUL!!! These cinnamon rolls were very quick and easy, the only changes I had to make were to add more flour (about a cup and a half or two cups) to keep it from being so sticky, and I added some cinnamon to the dough and about 1/4 cup sugar because I noticed the recipe didn't call for any. Also sugar helps the yeast proof faster. Since we love cinnamon, I put more into the brown sugar mix than the recipe called for. Also, I put them in the refrigerator overnight and they rose some, but not as much as I wanted so I let them rise in a warm place (the closet) for an hour before I baked them. The baking time was only 14 minutes for mine, and the cinnamon rolls were so perfect and golden and ENORMOUS! This recipe made 18 enormous cinnamon rolls. Seeing as it's only my mom and I, I'm going to give some to neighbors and friends. I topped them with homemade cream cheese frosting, but I don't think they needed it because they were already so moist and soft and wonderful. I don't think they were cakey or biscuity at all. As good as Cinnabon, just a lot cheaper! And if you crowd the pan a bit, the middles of the cinnamon rolls will come up just like Cinnabons. A couple tips: Warm the buttermilk over the lowest heat setting or it will start to curdle. Also, once you have your cinnamon roll log, stretch it out a bit if you need to to make it all the same thickness. I am down at our house on Mexico. I made some substitutions. I used one cup of whole wheat Sourdough Starter for leavening. I substituted one truncated cone of Peloncillo for the brown sugar. It was rock hard so I added the butter and a tablespoon of water to the bowl and microwaved for one minute. A fork was used to break up the lumps and to mix ground cinnamon into the butter and sugar. I cut salt down to 1/2 tsp.

The dough came out a little sticky so I added a little flour as kneaded, :). It turned out great.

I ground up three three inch sticks of common in the coffee grinder. Nice fresh aroma! 
It smelled so good. 
It came out perfect. I will make it again.

Delish! Added 1/2 cup white sugar to dry ingredients and increased cinnamon to 2-1/2 tsp; otherwise, assembled and cooked as written. (As always, it's important to hard-pack brown sugar when measuring.) Used plain dental floss to cut dough log into 20 1-inch pieces. Smeared cooked warm rolls with icing (blend to desired consistency a cube of butter with powdered sugar, vanilla, half & half).

These were pretty easy. I also used butter instead of oil and put a bit of sugar in the yeast. I only made a half recipe, but I still got a dozen cinnamon rolls out of it. 

I had a little trouble with the melted brown sugar and cinnamon getting too thick & found it was best to spread it with a rubber spatula instead of trying to brush it on. I found that it coagulated quickly and got hard to spread after a short time, so I sprinkled sugar and cinnamon in the bare spots. I think that next time, I'll mix white sugar with the brown sugar.

I made these the night before I wanted to eat them, so after I took them out of the refrigerator in the morning, I let them proof for about an hour and then baked them for about 20 minutes. They're so much better than the canned ones!

These were the best. We had our Christmas today due to work schedules. I try to make cinnamon rolls for Christmas breakfast- have tried different recipes- and this is by far the best. I made as written- I did not need any more flour, I made them the night before then put them in the fridge overnight. Then let rise this morning for an hour- turned my oven on for 2 minutes then turned it OFF for a warm rising spot. Baked at 375 so I wouldn't burn them for about 20-25 min. I put on a little bit of cream cheese frosting (though doesn't need this.) No filling oozing- except just the right amount in the bottom of the dish to scrape up-- light and flaky and a little moisty texture- 5 stars!!!!! The best! Had one with a cup of coffee then another with a glass of ice cold milk. Can't ask for more.

My first attempt at homemade cinnamon rolls and my family was impressed and enjoyed them very much! Directions were easy to follow. I used melted butter instead of vegetable oil and added 1 Tbsp sugar to the yeast and water mixture, but no other changes than those. I mixed these by hand and baked them the same morning I made them, but next time, I want to use my stand mixer and try the night-before method to save time in the morning. I also iced them with a cream cheese/butter icing recipe found on AR. Delicious!!

Loved it. Being a novice baker, I used our bread maker's dough setting because it's much easier and pretty much foolproof. I added an additional 1/4 cup of buttermilk, which I made using 1/2 & 1/2 and lemon juice, to replace the water. I sprinkled some chopped pecans on top of the cinnamon mixture before rolling, cutting and baking. Checked the first pan at 20 minutes, and they were overdone. Reduced that to 15 minutes afterwards which seemed to be about right. Delicious. Will definitely make these again.

These were absolutely wonderful! I made exactly as directed in the recipe with the exception of 2 additional Tbsp of flour before kneading the dough. I did invert my pan when these came out of the oven to get all of the delicious filling that had seeped out back on top of the rolls. I will 100% make this recipe again!

I just took these out of the oven. My wife ate two of them before I could glaze or take a picture of them. HA. They are outstanding. I followed the recipe exactly except I did add a tablespoon of sugar to the yeast mixture to help with proofing. I mixed everything in my Kitchen-aid with the dough hook no kneading. Then let them rest.

Also I cooked down two cups of Granny Smith apples with some cinnamon and sugar until they were soft. I lightly mashed them and spread a thin layer of that on top of the cinnamon and butter mix. Then I rolled and cut. I will definitely be making these again.

Following the recipe these turn out fluffy and tall. I’ve made more than once. Now I follow other reviews and add 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/4 c sugar to the dry ingredients. I also sprinkle some sugar to the water /yeast mixture to feed the yeast. For the filling I do not use melted butter, softened butter better. I also knead for ten minutes. Pairs nicely with The Perfect Cinnamon Roll Icing.

Absolutely ONE OF THE BEST recipes ever!! Ignore the poor ratings on these reviews!! If you follow the recipe it WILL turn out fine. This dough is NOT a traditional roll/bread dough and it IS stickier, but the 4.5 c of flour (King Arthur bread flour - always) is accurate. The only change I make (besides changing up the filling once in a while), is to use the microwave to heat the buttermilk & to add a tsp or Tbsp of sugar to more effectively proof the yeast!! .....I switched to this recipe over a year ago, after 30 years of using my family's cinnamon roll recipe (serious German bakers!)!! This is a recipe that IS ACCURATE, fast, consistent, can feed a crowd and is scrumptious!!!

This dough turned out very nice, tender and soft. I used a bread maker to make the dough, and removed from the bucket at 20 min. Into the rise function to roll out. I added soaked raisins to the filling and glazed with cinnamon glaze. Great tasting, delicate rolls. We will put this recipe in the rotation!
Beautiful ! Soft inside and a little crunchy out.
It was good, better once I adjusted for high altitudes! I backed off a little on the yeast and sugar and added a little more liquids, baked it hotter and faster, delicious
The dough was absolutely amazing. They are not the most cinnamon-y I've ever had but definitely very good.

This is the most amazing thing I have ever tasted. Followed measurements exactly. Made a few minor adjustments for instant yeast vs active dry. The solution for the sticky consistency that one user experienced is leaving it in the mixer longer to form stronger gluten bonds. One other note. If you steam bake at 350 for 20 minutes the texture is better than cinnabon.

This was a fast recipe to make. I did not add glaze to it like in the video, and it was perfect. I used powdered buttermilk and instant yeast instead of the fresh and active dry yeast as the recipe calls for respectively. Still, I warmed up the buttermilk prepared it according to the package and warmed it in the microwave until it reached 120F. I did have to use a bit of extra flour so the dough was not as sticky. I might not need the extra warm water next time if using instant yeast. Overall, great recipe and will make it again.
